title: The right to the act
situation: A man is about to do something that matters and cannot stop calculating how it will turn out.
wise_response: The verse separates the two: the act is his, the result is not. Do the work, give up the claim on its fruit, and do not use that as an excuse to do nothing.
why_it_worked: It removes the outcome from the ledger without removing the effort, so fear of failure stops being a reason to withhold action.
tempting_wrong_answer: Refuse to start until success is likely, or act only where the reward is visible.
original_text: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि
edition: Bhagavad Gita 2.47; Sanskrit from the gita/gita dataset (edition not stated)
ai_translation: Your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to inaction.

title: The self as friend or enemy
situation: A man keeps breaking his own resolutions and blames his circumstances.
wise_response: The verse tells him to lift himself by himself and not degrade himself: the self is the friend of the one who has mastered it, and the enemy of the one who has not.
why_it_worked: It puts the cause inside the person without excusing the circumstances, which is the only place he can actually act.
tempting_wrong_answer: Blame the conditions, or wait until he feels ready.
original_text:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः
बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः। अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्
edition: Bhagavad Gita 6.5-6.6; Sanskrit from the gita/gita dataset (edition not stated)
ai_translation: Lift yourself by yourself; do not let yourself fall. The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is its enemy. For him who has conquered himself by himself, the self is a friend; for him who has not, the self behaves as an enemy.

title: Friendliness to all beings
situation: A man has been wronged more than once and finds he has begun to resent people in general.
wise_response: The verse describes the one who is dear: hating no being, friendly and compassionate, without possessiveness or ego, equal in pain and pleasure, forgiving.
why_it_worked: It does not ask him to pretend the wrong did not happen. It asks him to stop letting the resentment become a general policy toward people.
tempting_wrong_answer: Turn the resentment into a rule: expect the worst of everyone and call it experience.
original_text: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च। निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी
edition: Bhagavad Gita 12.13; Sanskrit from the gita/gita dataset (edition not stated)
ai_translation: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free of possessiveness and ego, equal in pain and pleasure, and forgiving.
